question.text: Let the hyperbola <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>H</mi><mo>:</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>-</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> and the ellipse <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>E</mi><mo>:</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></math> be such that the length of latus rectum of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>H</mi></math> is equal to the length of latus rectum of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>E</mi></math>. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>H</mi></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>E</mi></msub></math> are the eccentricities of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>H</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>E</mi></math> respectively, then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>12</mn><mfenced><mrow><msubsup><mi>e</mi><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>e</mi><mi>E</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mfenced></math> is equal to _____.

solution.text:
Given

E≡3x2+4y2=12  ⇒ x24+y23=1

Now,  eE=1-b2a2=1-34=12

Length of L.R. =2b2a=2×32=3

Now H≡  x2a2-y21=1

 Length of L.R.=2b2a=2×1a

Given length of L.R. of E and H are equal

So 2a=3  ⇒  a=23

Now eH=b2a2+1=1232+1  ⇒  eH=94+1=134

So 12eH2+eE2=12134+14=12144=14×3=42
